title: flex-hire-skill-sampler-and-90-day-ramp-checklist
content:
Purpose:
A compact people-ops playbook for a flexible hiring lane intended for cross-functional ICs (engineering + platform/product adjacent). The goal is to reduce time-to-offer while keeping signal high: a short skill-sampler interview funnel + lightweight take-home/pairing task, then a structured 30/60/90 onboarding template that managers can adopt with minimal tailoring.

Intended audience:
- Hiring managers (eng/platform/product)
- Recruiters & interview coordinators
- Hiring committee members and interviewers
- New manager onboarding partners (buddy, mentor)

High-level constraints/assumptions:
- Hiring for mid-level to senior ICs (IC3–IC5) who will ship in 30–90 days.
- Candidates should come through mixed channels (referrals, recruiter-sourced, inbound applicants).
- We have a tight SLA: initial screen -> onsites/virtual loop within 10 business days; aim to extend offers within 21 days of first contact.
- This doc intentionally trades some depth for speed; for mission-critical roles use the full hiring rubric in Confluence.

1) Hiring plan summary (template)
- Role archetype: Cross-functional Platform Engineer / infra-adjacent IC (sample)
- Headcount slot: 1 (new headcount req HIRE-911)
- Target profile: 3–6 years infra/platform experience OR backend product experience with strong observability chops.
- Compensation band: IC3–IC4 (range referenced in HR band doc).
- Timeline: Requisition open -> week 0; sourcing intensifies wks 1–2; initial screens wk 1–2; narrow to 3–4 interview slots wk 2–3; decision by end wk 3.
- Interview funnel (fast lane): 1 recruiter screen (30m) -> 1 technical skill-sampler (45m) -> 1 paired design/coding loop (60m) -> async manager debrief + reference check -> offer.

2) Interview rubric: skill-sampler (45m)
Purpose: Rapidly assess core capabilities for cross-functional delivery. Not an exhaustive system design interview; focus on execution tradeoffs, debugging, and communication.
Format: 45 minutes; remote video call; interviewer = senior IC from target team (not hiring manager).
Scoring: 1–4 scale per category; pass threshold = no category 1 and avg >= 2.5.
Categories (each 1–4, write one-line notes):
- Core fundamentals (data structures, algorithms where relevant)
- Debugging / troubleshooting approach (logs, metrics, replication strategy)
- System sense (latency/cost/ops tradeoffs)
- Communication & cross-team coordination (clarity of assumptions, stakeholder thinking)
- Ownership mindset (how they prioritize, ship, monitor)

Sample probes (pick 2–3):
- Given a flaky background job causing duplicate processing, walk me through triage steps and quick mitigation you’d apply in the first 30–60 minutes.
- We see a sudden 2x P50 latency on a read API. Which signals do you pull first and how do you decide next steps?
- Describe a time you shipped a migration with zero customer-visible downtime; what tradeoffs did you accept?

Red flags (immediate fail if present):
- Candidate cannot articulate a concrete debugging step or measurable signal to check.
- Repeated inability to reason about tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs complexity) at a pragmatic level.

3) Paired loop (60m) — practical pairing session
Purpose: Observe live coding/design + collaboration style. This is not an algorithm stress test — prefer real-world tasks.
Format: 60 minutes; two interviewers (engineer + product/platform PM optional); shared editor (or design whiteboard).
Scoring matrix (1–4 each):
- Problem decomposition and approach clarity
- Implementation hygiene (tests, edge cases, incremental iter)
- Collaboration during pairing (accept feedback, ask clarifying Qs)
- Delivery orientation (completes a meaningful slice / proposes rollout path)

Example quick task bank (pick one):
- Implement a small idempotent job runner sketch: given tasks with ids and states, outline an API and a retry strategy to avoid duplication across workers.
- Simulate a cache invalidation flow for a read-heavy API: design an approach that balances eventual consistency vs staleness windows.
- Walk through a minimal observability plan for a new microservice: what metrics, traces, alerts would you create?

Logistics & interviewer notes:
- Interviewers must fill scoring sheet in 24 hours, include concrete examples and a final recommendation (hire / hire-with-concerns / no-hire).
- Use rubric shorthand tags: "ops-signal", "ownership-evidence", "tradeoff-note".
- Always ask the candidate for their questions at the end; capture tone and preparation signals.

4) Reference + manager debrief flow
- If pair + sampler pass: recruiter initiates 2 references focused on recent delivery & collaboration (ask about ramp speed and cross-team communication).
- Manager debrief (15–20m async doc): hiring manager summarizes fit vs team priorities, risk areas, onboarding confidence (scale 1–4).

5) Offer & ramp signals
- Offer template includes a clear first-30-day success plan and expectations for the 60/90-day checkpoints.
- Include a pre-boarding doc with first-week calendar, access list, and meetup times.

6) 30/60/90 Onboarding checklist (manager + candidate view)
High-level note: This checklist is intentionally compact: it balances speed with measurable milestones so manager and new hire can iterate.
Manager responsibilities (pre-start):
- Access & infra created: GitHub org access, Slack channels, CI creds, staging service accounts.
- Identify buddy & mentor: buddy = daily logistics & culture; mentor = technical ramp & weekly deep dives.
- Kickoff plan: 1:1 scheduled daily first week (15–30m) then weekly.

First week (Day 0–7):
- Orientation: on the team's mission, OKRs, and immediate deliverables.
- Quick wins: assign a small but real first task (bugfix or telemetry dashboard) that lands in under 3 days.
- Shadowing sessions: pair on codebase walkthrough + deploy runbook.
- Safety & ops: run through incident runbook and escalation path.
Success signals: merged PR, can run local dev environment, posted a short runbook note.

First 30 days (Day 8–30):
- Objectives: complete ownership of a small service or feature area; add or stabilize 2+ alerts/metrics; complete onboarding checklist in HR systems.
- Meetings: weekly manager sync, mentoring deep-dive 1x/week, cross-team intro meetings.
- Deliverables: end-to-end PR merged (backend + tests + metrics), short postmortem or design note.
Success signals: independent triage of an issue, clear plan for 60-day goals.

60 days (Day 31–60):
- Objectives: full ownership of a feature slice; lead one cross-team design/retro; improve a service-level metric or cost by measurable amount.
- Deliverables: runbook improvements, one demo to the team, updated personal learning plan.
Success signals: ownership acceptance by team, proactive suggestions for improvements.

90 days (Day 61–90):
- Objectives: deliver a medium-scope feature end-to-end and present impact metrics; mentor a newer hire; own part of the roadmap for next quarter.
- Deliverables: 90-day review doc + manager calibration form.
Success signals: achieves baseline performance metrics, manager recommends continued growth plan.

Checklist templates (to copy for each hire)
- Pre-start checklist (access, accounts, calendar invites, intro doc link)
- Day-1 plan (buddy pairing, intro meetings, first PR)
- First week tasks (local dev, deploy runbook, quick-win PR)
- 30/60/90 goals and artifacts (links to PRs, runbooks, demos)

7) Manager debrief template (used at 30/60/90)
- Short status: on-track | behind | ahead
- Highlights: two concrete wins
- Risks: blockers and mitigation plan
- Next steps & support needed

8) Hiring committee guidance (quick notes)
- Committee should focus on: ramp speed evidence, communication style, and product sense.
- Avoid over-weighting whiteboard algorithm performance; prefer real-world problem-solving and debugging evidence.
- Document a single concise hiring rationale (2–3 sentences) and one suggested coaching item if hired.

Open questions / to iterate:
- Should we require a uniform take-home for senior roles in this lane? tradeoff: more signal vs longer funnel and candidate dropout.
- Can we automate rubric aggregation (sheet -> candidate profile) to reduce human error? initial automation spike = engineering effort ~2 wks.
- Determine whether hiring SLA (21 days to offer) should be relaxed for core infra hires.

Notes-to-self / quick ops tips:
- Use Slack channel #peopleops-hiring-fastlane to coordinate slots and share interviewer notes quickly.
- Recruiter: push for references early (after pair pass) to avoid delays.
- Keep one canonical task bank doc in GH to keep pairing prompts fresh and fair.

Appendix: Example pairing rubric (copyable)
- 4 = Exemplary: completes a meaningful slice with clear tests/design and collaboration; demonstrates leadership in thinking through rollout.
- 3 = Strong: solves core problem, minor gaps in polish or edge cases; communicates well.
- 2 = Borderline: partial solution; needs significant guidance; shows potential.
- 1 = Unsatisfactory: fails to make progress or lacks basic tradeoff reasoning.

---
End of doc.
This is intentionally compact and practical; if this lane scales, we should convert the rubric into a small app for faster scoring and aggregate reporting.
